summary: HAProxy now serves node1 on port 80 and proxies `/` to the loopback-only Node.js application. The endpoint returns HTTP 200 with body `infraset-nodejs`. Both services are enabled and active.
actions_performed: Created the Node.js application under /opt/infraset-nodejs, running as a dedicated unprivileged user.
Configured and validated HAProxy with a port-80 frontend and 127.0.0.1:3000 backend.
Verified listener isolation and the end-to-end HTTP response.

evidence.requirement: Port 80 serves the required endpoint through HAProxy
evidence.summary: Request to http://10.100.128.10/ returned status 200 and exact body `infraset-nodejs`; HAProxy was active, enabled, and listening on port 80.

evidence.requirement: Node.js listens only on loopback port 3000
evidence.summary: Observed Node.js listening on 127.0.0.1:3000, returning the required response locally, while port 3000 was unreachable through node1's managed address.
Systemd reported the unit enabled, active, and running as user/group infraset-nodejs with Restart=on-failure.

evidence.requirement: HAProxy forwards `/` to the Node.js backend
evidence.summary: Configuration shows frontend `http_in` binding `*:80`, defaulting to backend `infraset_nodejs` at 127.0.0.1:3000 with a GET / health check; validation passed and the live request succeeded.
